messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (us-west). p95=820ms (SLO=250ms), p99=2.4s (SLO=1s). Streaming stalls spike: 6% of streams showing >10s stall. Affected routes: generate-long-context, streaming-chat. Alert: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/alerts/metric/5160000000

alex: ack, I'm oncall. Paging now. Any customer reports?

maria: I see increased KV cache eviction rate and slab churn in the runtime. Prefill-heavy workloads spiking memory pressure, decode side is starving and causing tail stalls. Graphed in the prefills panel: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/prefill/kv-slabs?from=now-30m&to=now

alex: good. Quick checks: 1) confirm scope (which models/routes) 2) mitigation plan 3) notify impacted customers

jordan: looks concentrated on generate-long-context (seq>32k) and a handful of enterprise keys. AcmeCorp telemetry shows streaming stalls and a small spike in 502s correlated with the same window.

maria: quick diagnostic dump: `redwoodctl metrics query --name runtime.kv.evictions --window 10m --agg=sum` -> output:
```
runtime.kv.evictions  12730
runtime.kv.slabs_in_use  213
runtime.kv.avg_fragmentation 0.72
runtime.kv.prefill_rate  185/s
runtime.kv.decode_rate   42/s
```
The prefill:decode ratio is ~4.4x for the past 12 minutes. That matches prefill-dominant workload filling slabs unevenly.

alex: so prefill-heavy requests are pushing out useful decode entries -> tail stalls when decode needs KV entries. Any fast mitigations?

maria: proposing hot mitigations: A) throttle prefill for long-context routes, B) trigger slab compaction/purge on least-recently-used segments, C) temporary routing fallback to smaller-model quantized variant for enterprise customers, D) raise KV memory quota as a short-term scale.

ops-bot: NOTE: Autoscaler recommending +2 worker pods in us-west pool due to mem pressure. (action required: authorize scale).

alex: Authorize +2 pods for now to reduce pressure. jordan please approv? @jordan

jordan: approve scale, doing `kubectl scale deployment/runtime-us-west --replicas=20`. Also enabling conservative streaming fallback for AcmeCorp: route them to model-redwood-lite/high-latency-fallback.

maria: applying hot config to reduce prefill aggressiveness on long-route: 
```
# hotfix
redwoodctl config set --route generate-long-context --kv.prefill.enabled=false --kv.prefill.weight=0.2
redwoodctl config set --global runtime.kv.slab_compaction=true --global runtime.kv.compaction_target=0.65
```

maria: kicked slab compaction run across shards (job id compaction-516000) and evicted low-hit-rate prefixes. Also forced immediate reclaim on two highest-fragmentation nodes.

incident-bot: Action logged: scale +2 pods, config change applied (generate-long-context kv.prefill=false), slab compaction job started.

alex: notify customers: Jordan/CS, ping AcmeCorp CSM with mitigation note. Jordan can you send quick note?

jordan: pinged AcmeCorp, response: "Thanks — we see degraded streaming UX, appreciate quick mitigation." CSM will monitor.

maria: post-mitigation metrics snapshot (5m after changes):
```
runtime.kv.evictions  3140
runtime.kv.avg_fragmentation 0.48
runtime.kv.prefill_rate  62/s
runtime.kv.decode_rate   58/s
p95 /v1/generate  160ms
p99 /v1/generate  420ms
streaming_stalls_rate  0.8%
```

alex: good improvement. Keep monitoring for 30m. If numbers hold, we can roll back temporary scale later.

maria: note: we saw one node with persistent slab fragmentation due to a very large single-customer prefix (AcmeCorp long-history). I created a remediation ticket to implement per-prefix eviction caps and smarter LRU across prefill/decode.

jordan: FYI ops: need follow-ups: 1) add prefill:decode ratio alert (threshold 2.0), 2) surface slab fragmentation % per-shard in SLO dashboards, 3) plan a capacity bump for us-west reserved pool.

alex: oncall handoff: I'm handing to maria for monitoring and immediate follow-up. maria, you own until 5160002160 (end of shift). jordan will coordinate customer comms and postmortem.

maria: taking over. Monitoring runs: aggregated p95 steady at ~150-180ms for 15m, p99 ~410-480ms, streaming stalls down to baseline but still watching. If p99 exceeds 700ms or streaming stalls >2% we re-open.

ops-bot: Reminder: incident severity auto-classified as Sev2. Please attach runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.local/pages/kv-fragmentation-runbook

alex: quick note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = sudden surge of very long-context prefill-heavy requests from enterprise customers causing KV slab fragmentation and eviction cascade; decode entries starving leading to tail latency and streaming stalls. Short term mitigations: throttle prefill, slab compaction, scale pods, route to fallback models. Long-term actions: per-prefix caps, rebalancing heuristics, better metrics/alerts, possible change to prefill policy.

maria: creating follow-up tickets: R-1234 (prefill heuristics), R-1235 (per-prefix eviction cap), R-1236 (dashboarding slab fragmentation).

incident-bot: Incident state: MONITORING. p95=170ms, p99=430ms, streaming_stalls=0.7%. Will auto-check in 30m.

alex: closing active paging. If anyone sees regression reactivate. Great job team. :thumbsup:

maria: acknowledged, will keep an eye and add notes to the pm.

jordan: I'll draft postmortem and customer-facing summary.

incident-bot: Incident resolved? Please update severity and assign postmortem owner.

maria: postmortem owner assigned: jordan. Severity final: Sev2. Closing thread but leaving linked tickets open.
